summary: Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1994–2001) and Harvard University (~2001–2009). She held a post at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

Akimichi Eda is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. from the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar.
Akio Donohashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1977) and served as a professor at Kobe University from 1990 to 1991.

Akio Tanabe works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–2006). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993), Kyoto University (1998, 2004), and the University of Tokyo (professor in 2015).

Akira Fujieda specialized in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1931–1934), he worked at its Institute for Research in Humanities, Northwest Institute, and as professor at Kyoto University (1968).

Akira Hirakawa was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (1939–1941, ~1954–1959) under Shoson Miyamoto. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1954–1975) and taught at Waseda University (1975–1985).

Akira Miyaji specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his degrees at Nagoya University (~1964–1991) and held posts at Hirosaki University, Nagoya University (~1976–2007), Shizuoka Prefectural Museum of Art, and Ryukoku University (2013).

Akira Mukai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral coursework at Hokkaido University, where he served as an assistant (~1974–1980), and was later a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

Akira Omine worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Kyoshi Takahama and at Heidelberg University. He held positions at Kyoto University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University (1980–1992), and Ryukoku University.

Akira Sadakata is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1955–1959) under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, and at the University of Paris (1963). He was a professor at Tokai University (~1976–2002).

Akira Saito specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikidō Takasaki and at the Australian National University. His posts include the University of Tokyo (2000–2016) and International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Akira Shimada is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, under Rajeev Lochan and Daud Ali. He held posts at the British Museum and the State University of New York.

Akira Suganuma was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1959–1962), where he served as an assistant (~1962–1967) and associate professor (1991–1994). He also taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Akira Takeda was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (1949–1959) under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held academic posts at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (~1959–1968), the University of Tokyo (assistant 1961, professor 1965–1991), and Meikai University.

Akira Yuyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Naoshiro Tsuji, Akira Hirakawa, Jan Willem de Jong, and Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He directed the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and held professorships at Soka University.
Akitoshi Saito is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Taisho University as professor (attested 1982) and professor emeritus (attested 2014).
Akshay Ramanlal Desai was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Mumbai from ~1937 to 1946 under the supervision of Govind Sadashiv Ghurye.

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Temple University (attested 1988) and held academic posts in the Department of Philosophy at the University of Delaware.

Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under Parimal G. Patil, and also studied under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.
Alan Gowans was a scholar of history and archaeology. He pursued his higher education at the University of Toronto (1946) and Princeton University (1948, 1950).
